# Sirach Chapter 29 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 29 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

**29:1** He-who-shows-mercy will-lend to-his-neighbor, and he-who-strengthens-him-with-his-hand keeps the-commandments.

**29:2** Lend to-your-neighbor in-the-time-of-his-need, and in-return pay-back your-neighbor in-his-time.

**29:3** Keep your-word and deal-faithfully with-him, and at-every-time you-will-find what-you-need.

**29:4** Many have-treated a-loan as a-windfall, and caused-grief to-those-who-helped-them.

**29:5** Until-he-receives he-kisses-the-hands of-his-neighbor, and in-his-voice he-humbles-himself concerning his-neighbor's-money; but at-the-time-of-repayment he-postpones and returns-words-of-complaint and blames the-time.

**29:6** If-he-is-able, he-will-scarcely-repay-half, and-he-will-count-it-as-a-windfall; if-not, he-will-rob-him of-his-money, and he-will-acquire-him-as-an-enemy gratuitously. He-will-repay him with-abuse and insults, and instead-of honor he-will-repay him with-dishonor.

**29:7** Many — not from-wickedness — have-refused-to-lend; they-were-afraid of-being-wronged gratuitously.

**29:8** Nevertheless, toward-the-lowly be-long-suffering, and do-not-make-him-wait for-your-alms.

**29:9** For-the-sake of-the-commandment help-the-poor, and according-to his-need do-not-send-him-away-empty.

**29:10** Lose-your-silver on-behalf-of a-brother and a-friend, and do-not-let-it-rust under a-stone for-loss.

**29:11** Lay-up your-treasure according-to the-commandments of-the-Most-High, and it-will-profit you more-than gold.

**29:12** Lock-up almsgiving in your-storerooms, and it-will-rescue-you from every-trouble.

**29:13** More-than a-mighty-shield and more-than a-heavy-spear, it-will-fight on-your-behalf against an-enemy.

**29:14** A-good-man will-stand-as-surety for-his-neighbor, and he-who-has-lost-his-sense-of-shame will-abandon-him.

**29:15** Do-not-forget the-good-deeds of-your-guarantor, for he-has-given-his-life for-you.

**29:16** The-sinful-man will-ruin the-goods of-his-guarantor,

**29:17** and the-ungrateful in-his-soul will-abandon the-one-who-rescued him.

**29:18** Going-surety has-ruined many-who-were-prosperous, and has-shaken-them as a-sea-wave; powerful-men has-it-made-wander, and they-have-wandered among foreign-nations.

**29:19** A-sinner who-falls-into-surety and who-undertakes-contracts on-his-behalf will-fall-into-lawsuits.

**29:20** Help-your-neighbor according-to your-power, and take-heed to-yourself lest you-fall.

**29:21** The-essentials of-life are water and bread and clothing and a-house to-cover-the-nakedness [of-one].

**29:22** Better-is-the-life of a-poor-man under a-roof of-logs than dainty-meals in-another-man's-house among-strangers.

**29:23** With-little or-with-much, be-well-satisfied; and you-will-not-hear the-reproach-of-being-a-stranger.

**29:24** It-is-a-miserable-life going-from-house-to-house, and where you-are-a-stranger you-dare-not-open-your-mouth.

**29:25** You-will-play-the-host and will-pour-out drink-without-gratitude; and in-addition you-will-hear-bitter-words:

**29:26** "Come-here, stranger, set a-table, and if-you-have-anything-on-hand, feed-me."

**29:27** "Go-away, stranger, from the-face of-honor; a-guest is-here; my-brother has-come and I-need the-place."

**29:28** Hard for a-man of-good-nature is reproach concerning going-and-coming and lending and moneylending.
